args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1, with an error rate of ~18%. The deploy history shows v2.3.1 as unhealthy; v2.3.0 was the most recent version healthy in production, so a rollback to v2.3.0 was initiated across all production regions.

The first rollout attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet in a mixed state: us-east on v2.3.0, while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry of the same rollback completed successfully, and all three regions are now on v2.3.0. Post-rollback verification shows the service healthy with an error rate of approximately 0.2%.

Note: v2.3.1-rc is listed in the release history as unhealthy but is a staging deployment and was not involved in production. It's worth investigating whether the issues in the rc were carried into the v2.3.1 production release. Follow-up: root-cause analysis of the v2.3.1 failure before any re-attempt to roll it forward.

trace.final:
The incident was in fact created as **INC-0001** — the timeout was on the response, not the operation. No retry needed (and the idempotency key would have made one harmless anyway).

## Summary

**Root cause / state found:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), failing health checks with an ~18% error rate. Release history confirmed v2.3.1 as unhealthy and showed **v2.3.0** as the most recent release healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc also shows unhealthy but is a staging deployment, so it was correctly not a rollback candidate.)

**Rollback:** Rolled back to v2.3.0 across all production regions.
- First attempt failed with `partial_failure`: orchestrator error halted the rollout after us-east, leaving a **mixed fleet** (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west still on v2.3.1). I verified this state rather than assuming success or failure.
- Retried the same rollback to v2.3.0; it completed with `status: rolled_out` in all three regions.

**Verification:** Service now reports version v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west, `healthy: true`, error rate down from 18% to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on checkout-api. The summary documents the v2.3.1 failure, the correct rollback target and rationale, the partial-failure/mixed-state episode and its resolution, and the post-rollback healthy verification. It also flags two follow-ups: whether the staging v2.3.1-rc problems carried into the production v2.3.1 build, and the need for root-cause analysis before any attempt to roll v2.3.1 forward again.

No approval was required — v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production, so this was a rollback to a known-good version rather than deploying a never-healthy version.

One note for the team: the rollback tool's partial-failure behavior means a single failed rollout can leave regions on divergent versions. Worth checking service status after any rollback rather than treating the call as atomic.
